messages:
maria (eng-security): heads-up — found a small plaintext file from a recent nightly backup in /tmp on backup-agent-12 during a retry. looks like agent retried and wrote a temp file before encrypting. not widespread but need triage.
kevin (eng-sre): yikes. any evidence it got uploaded to S3?
maria (eng-security): checking logs now — agent uploaded object key `backups/db/2026-03-20/part-0003.tmp` then renamed to `.enc` after encrypt step, but we have a window where the temp existed locally. CloudTrail shows PutObject succeeded for the .tmp key for ~5s.
kevin (eng-sre): can you paste the log snippet?
maria (eng-security): sure —
```
2026-03-20T02:11:03Z INFO backup-agent: preparing shard /var/tmp/backup/part-0003.tmp
2026-03-20T02:11:08Z WARN backup-agent: upload start key=backups/db/2026-03-20/part-0003.tmp
2026-03-20T02:11:13Z INFO kms: encrypt start key=backups/db/2026-03-20/part-0003.tmp
2026-03-20T02:11:15Z INFO backup-agent: rename key -> part-0003.enc
```
kevin (eng-sre): ok so S3 had the tmp key for a few seconds. do we have lifecycle rules to delete `*.tmp`?
alex (eng-platform): not currently. we treat tmp keys as ephemeral but we don't enforce server-side deletion.
sasha (backup-agent): this is from an edge case — retry path writes temp file, calls PutObject (to avoid losing data mid-stream), then attempts client-side encryption; failure here is that we upload before encryption. agent code should stream-encrypt locally into tempfile `.enc` and then upload. i'll open a patch.
maria (eng-security): immediate actions: 1) confirm whether tmp key still present in prod bucket; 2) if present, copy to secure audit bucket and mark for forensic, then delete original; 3) rotate agent credentials that touched this run; 4) update runbook.
kevin (eng-sre): running S3 list now — `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-backups-prod --prefix backups/db/2026-03-20/ --query 'Contents[?contains(Key, `.tmp`)]..Key'`
kevin (eng-sre): looks like one tmp key exists still. taking object lock snapshot and copying to `s3://redwood-forensics/encops-temp/1769234567/` then will delete original.
eng-sec-oncall: please post the object metadata and S3 server-side encryption headers before deletion (want to confirm SSE-KMS vs SSE-S3).
kevin (eng-sre): metadata: `{"x-amz-server-side-encryption":"AES256","x-amz-meta-uploader":"backup-agent-12"}` so it was uploaded with SSE-S3, not KMS.
maria (eng-security): that raises a policy gap — uploader role should not be allowed to use SSE-S3 for customer backups. we should require SSE-KMS with our CMK and require encryption context.
alex (eng-platform): agreed. current uploader IAM allows `s3:PutObject` and `s3:PutObjectAcl` and is able to supply `x-amz-server-side-encryption`. we can tighten. proposed policy snippet:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-backups-prod/backups/*"],
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"},
    "StringEqualsIfExists": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/our-cmk"}
  }
}
```
kevin (eng-sre): also drop `s3:PutObjectAcl` unless we explicitly need it. that prevents accidental public ACLs.
sasha (backup-agent): patch incoming — modify agent so encryption happens before any PutObject; fallback path will abort upload instead of uploading tmp. i'll send a PR.
maria (eng-security): audit logging: CloudTrail currently shows PutObject but not KMS:Encrypt calls for SSE-S3 (there were none). we need a CloudTrail filter/alert for PutObject where `x-amz-server-side-encryption` != `aws:kms` for backup prefixes. add to detection rules.
eng-sec-oncall: adding rule to sigma: `eventName: PutObject AND requestParameters.bucketName: redwood-backups-prod AND NOT requestParameters.headers.x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` -> high-priority. also add an alert when PutObject occurs with key suffix `.tmp`.
kevin (eng-sre): done. CloudWatch alarm created and SNS hook to #incidents if matched.
maria (eng-security): vuln triage note: this is a design flaw in agent write-order, not present in all versions. severity: medium (data exposure window small) but treat as P0 for fix + creds rotation.
sasha (backup-agent): PR: https://github.com/redwood/backup-agent/pull/482 — adds pre-encrypt step, removes tmp upload path, and adds integration test to fail if a `.tmp` object is observed in S3 during CI.
alex (eng-platform): ops change: rolling update to backup-agent fleet with deploy tokens — we should stage to canary pool first. can we automatic rollback if detect tmp uploads? sre-bot can watch S3.
sre-bot: deploy started to canary group `backup-canary-1` — will monitor for `*.tmp` PutObject events for 30m.\e ng-sec-oncall: also recommend we modify KMS key policy to reject requests that do not include expected encryption context "purpose":"backup" for decrypt/encrypt. that provides defense-in-depth.
maria (eng-security): yes — update CMK policy + enforce in agent with `EncryptionContext` on GenerateDataKey/Encrypt. add check in restore pipeline to fail if encryption context mismatch.
kevin (eng-sre): quick mechanical tasks done: copied object to forensics bucket, deleted tmp key, rotated the service account creds for backup-agent-12, kicked off scrubbing job to check for other tmp keys in last 7 days.
eng-sec-oncall: adding playbook entries: 1) immediate containment steps, 2) evidence preservation (copy to forensics), 3) cred rotation guidance, 4) KMS/ACL policy tightening, 5) CI test coverage. linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backup-encops — will update section 3.
maria (eng-security): steps for next 48h: - merge agent patch and roll canary - update uploader IAM policy (condition to require KMS) - add CloudTrail/CloudWatch detectors - update CMK policy for encryption context - run retrospective to see if any customer data could have been exposed (low likelihood)\e ng-sec-oncall: i'll schedule a short postmortem tomorrow 9:30am PT; invite list: eng-security, eng-sre, eng-platform, backup-agent owners, legal.
kevin (eng-sre): note for compliance: add audit log entry with object ETag and requestId before deletion so we can meet audit requirements.
maria (eng-security): good call. posting that here for record. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
kevin (eng-sre): thanks — monitoring the canary now.
sasha (backup-agent): will patch and publish a minor release, CCing release notes about the encryption-before-upload change.
maria (eng-security): closing initial thread — will attach postmortem link after meeting.
eng-sec-oncall: incident ticket created: INC-2026-0422 — tracking remediation and runbook updates.
